column1: # The normalization table of the parity harness (ADR-0022),
# read by scripts/check-parity.sh. One row per bash message, three or four fields separated by tabs: an
# extended regular expression the message after "  - " matches; the rule ID of nuc it maps to;
# "line" when the bash message names a line, "-" when it names none and the comparison leaves the
# line out; and "=<path>" for the file nuc names in place of the bash's location, or "+<prefix>"
# before it. A rule's first row sets the mode for all its findings. A bash message no row matches
# is a difference, so a ported rule brings its rows, and a check that is not ported yet is caught
# when it fires on a tree of the corpus.
# check-docs.sh, check 14: the template release named.
^README\.md: no '\*\*Template release:\*\*' line
^README\.md: the Template release line names neither
# check-docs.sh, check 1: the ADR index.
^ADR index not found: docs/adr/README\.md$
^ADR index: row for [^ ]+ links to
^ADR index: row for [^ ]+ is .+ but sits (above|below) the 'Superseded and rejected' heading
^ADR index: lists '.*' twice
^ADR index: file '.*' exists but is not listed in the index$
^ADR index: lists '.*', but no such ADR file exists$
^ADR index: status for '.*' is .* in the index but .* in the file$
^ADR index: 'Applies to' for '.*' is '.*' in the index but '.*' in the file$
^[^ :]+: no '\*\*Status:\*\*' line with a status emoji found$
^[^ :]+: no '\*\*Applies to:\*\*' line naming what the decision constrains$
# check-docs.sh, check 2: the ADR numbering.
^ADR numbering: expected '[0-9]{4}-\*\.md' at position [0-9]+, found
^[^ :]+: heading says '.*', but the filename says ADR-
^[^ :]+: a draft's slug is lower case letters and digits joined by single hyphens$
# check-docs.sh, check 7: the ADR headers; the stray field names its line, the others none.
^[^ :]+:[0-9]+: a header field not written as the list item
^[^ :]+: status line carries [0-9]+ status emoji
^[^ :]+: status line reads
^[^ :]+: still carries the instruction paragraph from template\.md
# check-docs.sh, check 5: the ADR references.
^[^:]+:[0-9]+: reference '.*' matches no ADR file in docs/adr/$
# check-docs.sh, check 6: a link citing an ADR points at its file.
^[^:]+: link '.*' cites ADR-.* but points at '.*'$
# check-docs.sh, check 8: the supersessions.
^[^ :]+: [^ :]+ supersedes it, but its status line does not say 'superseded by ADR-
^[^ :]+: status is ⚪ but the line names no superseding ADR$
^[^ :]+: [^ :]+ says it supersedes, but it carries no '\*\*Supersedes:\*\*' field naming ADR-
^[^ :]+: superseded by ADR-[^ ]+, which is not accepted — the status line flips when the human accepts ADR-
# check-docs.sh, check 3: the relative links.
^[^:]+: broken relative link -> '.*'$
^[^:]+: link '.*' has no matching anchor '#.*' in .*$
# check-docs.sh, check 4: the section references; the findings of AGENTS.md itself name no line.
^[^:]+:[0-9]+: reference 'AGENTS\.md, section [0-9]+' matches no numbered section in AGENTS\.md$
^[^:]+:[0-9]+: reference '§[0-9]+' matches no numbered section in AGENTS\.md$
^[^:]+:[0-9]+: '§[0-9]+' is cited without an anchor
^[^:]+:[0-9]+: '§[0-9]+' stands outside a link
^AGENTS\.md not found in the repository root$
^AGENTS\.md: no numbered '## N\.' section headings found$
^AGENTS\.md: numbered sections must run 1\.\.N in order
# check-docs.sh, check 9: the check lists.
^[^:]+: not found — the check lists cannot be compared$
^scripts/check-all\.sh: '# Not a gate: .*' names (the workflow of the required checks|no workflow of this repository)$
^[^:]+: job '[^']*' runs no script under scripts/ — the local gate cannot run what it does$
^\.github/workflows/checks\.yml: no jobs found under 'jobs:'
^scripts/check-all\.sh: no 'run <label> <script>' invocations found
^scripts/check-all\.sh: (does not run|runs) '.*', which (a workflow runs|no job of a workflow runs) — CI and the local gate disagree$
^scripts/[^:]+: no workflow and not scripts/check-all\.sh runs it
^README\.md: no job names between the 'required-checks' markers
^README\.md: required check '.*' (is not a job of|is a job with a matrix|names a check run of)
^README\.md: job '.*' of .* is missing from the required checks
# check-docs.sh, check 10: the Project Layout.
^README\.md: not found — the Project Layout block cannot be checked$
^README\.md: Project Layout lists '.*', which (matches nothing|is not a directory|does not exist)
^README\.md: no paths found under '## Project Layout'
^README\.md: Project Layout does not name '.*', a top-level part of this repository$
# check-docs.sh, check 11: the skill pointers.
^\.claude/skills/[^:]+: (is a copy of the skill|no pointer|is not a symlink into|dangles|points at )
# check-docs.sh, check 12: the inherited ADRs decided.
^[^ :]+: inherited from the template and (not decided by this project|still proposed after setup) —
# check-docs.sh, check 13: the template's identity replaced.

^README\.md: (the title is still the template's|the intro still explains the template's name|the Why NUC section still presents the template|the Overview is still the scaffold's sentence|the Usage section is still TODO|a badge still points at the template's repository|a Build, Test, Lint, or Run command is still TODO)
^\.devcontainer/devcontainer\.json: the Dev Container still carries the template's name$
^LICENSE: the copyright holder is still the placeholder
^SECURITY\.md: the security contact is still the placeholder$
^CODE_OF_CONDUCT\.md: the reporting contact is still the placeholder$
^\.github/CODEOWNERS: (no active rule|the instruction to add a code owner is still there)
^docs/[A-Z]+\.md: (the title still carries '<Project Name>'|a criterion is still the scaffold's placeholder|the scaffold's (building block|entry) is still listed)
# check-docs.sh, check 15: the prose width.
^[^:]+:[0-9]+: [0-9]+ columns — wrap the prose at 100 \(a link that does not fit stands on a line of its own\)$
# check-docs.sh, check 16: no draft on main.
^[^ :]+: a draft lands on main — give it its number first with scripts/number-adrs\.sh \(ADR-0002\)$
# check-traceability.sh, part 1: the criteria of the specification.
^docs/SPECIFICATION\.md: not found — the criteria cannot be read$
^docs/SPECIFICATION\.md: '[GQ]-[0-9]+' is listed under the wrong section —
^docs/SPECIFICATION\.md: identifier '[GQ]-[0-9]+' appears twice —
^docs/SPECIFICATION\.md: list item without a bold [GQ]-n identifier:
# check-traceability.sh, parts 2 to 4: not ported yet, left out of the comparison.
^docs/adr/[^ :]+: 'Not mechanically decidable' declared without a reason —
^[^ :]+:[0-9]+: cites '[^']+', which (does not exist in docs/adr/|is superseded or rejected — |is not a criterion of docs/SPECIFICATION\.md)
^ADR-[0-9]{4} is accepted but no test cites it —
